about.title: Mission Viejo Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Mission Viejo walk into a clinic, urgent care, or hospital expecting to leave better than they arrived. Usually that is what happens. Sometimes it does not, and the reason is not bad luck but a provider who fell below the standard of care that a reasonably careful doctor, nurse, or pharmacist would have met. That distinction matters. California law is clear that a disappointing result by itself is not malpractice; there has to be a proven error and a link between that error and the harm. Proving it takes records, a timeline, and almost always the opinion of a qualified medical expert. It also takes speed, because under MICRA you generally have one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it occurred, with a 90-day notice owed to the provider before filing. In a city of roughly 97,000 residents where many families rely on the same handful of medical offices along Marguerite Parkway and nearby corridors, we help you reach an independent attorney who can review what happened. There is no charge for the connection, and network attorneys work on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Mission Viejo Patients Use LawProactive

items.title: MICRA deadlines are short and layered
items.desc: One year from discovery, a hard three-year outer limit, and a 90-day pre-suit notice can overlap in confusing ways. Getting connected early gives your attorney room to work inside those windows.

items.title: Expert review comes first
items.desc: Nearly every California malpractice claim needs a qualified medical expert to say the standard of care was breached. Attorneys in our network know how to arrange that review before anyone commits to a lawsuit.

items.title: Damages are calculated, not guessed
items.desc: MICRA caps non-economic damages, and that cap increases every year. An attorney who tracks the current figure can explain realistically what parts of your loss are limited and which, like medical bills and lost income, are not.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on I-5 near Mission Viejo, then my treatment made things worse. Are those separate claims?
items.answer: They can be. Mission Viejo recorded 210 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those patients later experienced errors in follow-up care. The driver's liability and the provider's liability are evaluated separately, with different deadlines and proof requirements, so it helps to have an attorney look at both at once.

items.question: My surgery did not fix the problem. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not by itself. California requires a showing that the provider did something a competent provider would not have done, and that this caused your harm. A poor outcome after appropriate care is not a claim, which is why an expert's review of your records is the real first step.

items.question: How long do I have to act in Orange County?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from the injury itself. Before filing, the provider must receive 90 days' notice of your intent to sue. Because those clocks interact, it is wise to speak with an attorney as soon as you suspect something went wrong.
